drivers: Recovery balance not provided, but ACWR cannot be calculated due to missing acute/chronic load metrics — critical gap; HRV data absent, so no baseline comparison; resting HR data absent; training readiness not provided; only 1 run in September vs 10 in August suggests abrupt drop-off likely due to fatigue or illness; recent runs show elevated aerobic TE (3.5 on 8.9 km, 3.3 on 4.0 km) — above 3.0 indicates aerobic strain; ground contact time spiked to 385 ms on 8.23 (vs median ~295–305 ms), consistent with fatigue-induced gait deterioration
readiness.guidance: The athlete is not recovered enough for structured intensity or volume increase; priority is rest, sleep hygiene, and low-stimulus movement.

monthly_review.summary: Running volume collapsed from 51.3 km in August to just 5.0 km in September, with pace slowing significantly and zone distribution shifting heavily toward Z2 — indicating either forced reduction or loss of capacity.
monthly_review.highlight: The 12.4 ml/kg/km efficiency this month is the lowest (best) value in the entire 5-month history — a meaningful improvement — but it occurred during a single 5.0 km run at very slow pace (9:36/km), suggesting reduced neuromuscular demand rather than true physiological gain.

goal_tracker.message: Catching up would require ~46 km across 9 sessions (~5.1 km/session) in 29 days — but readiness is compromised, aerobic TE is elevated in recent longer efforts, and cadence dropped sharply, indicating fatigue. Chasing last month’s volume is medically inadvisable and risks injury or burnout.

insights.title: Efficiency improved only under low-load conditions
insights.body: Best efficiency (12.4 ml/kg/km) occurred during the sole September run — a 5.0 km effort at 9:36/km (576 sec/km) and HR 140, well below lactate threshold; contrast with August’s best efficiency (14.12) achieved across higher-volume, mixed-intensity work — suggesting the 'improvement' reflects deconditioning, not adaptation.

insights.title: Fatigue visibly altered gait mechanics
insights.body: Ground contact time jumped from median ~295–305 ms to 385 ms on 8.23 (slow 10:51/km pace), while vertical oscillation dropped to 6.6 mm — classic signs of reduced leg spring and compensatory shuffling gait under fatigue.

insights.title: Z3 work disappeared while Z2 dominance increased
insights.body: Z3 % dropped from 26% in August to 16% in September, while Z2 rose from 22% to 82%; this extreme polarisation — without Z1 recovery work (only 2% Z1) — suggests accumulated fatigue prevented sustaining even moderate intensities, not intentional polarised training.

recommendations.action: Complete full rest (no running) on Tuesday and Thursday; walk 30 min at <100 bpm on Wednesday and Saturday.
recommendations.reason: Cadence dropped 11 spm, ground contact increased 80+ ms, and aerobic TE remains >3.0 in recent long efforts — all indicate systemic fatigue requiring unload.

recommendations.action: Zone 1 easy run: 3.5 km, HR ≤125 bpm, cadence ≥145 spm, on Sunday — stop immediately if HR exceeds 128 or cadence falls below 140.
recommendations.reason: To test autonomic resilience and reinforce efficient stride before reintroducing stimulus; Z1 was nearly absent (2%) this month, increasing decoupling risk.

recommendations.action: Perform daily 10-min HRV-guided box breathing (4-4-4-4) after waking, tracking subjective energy and morning HR if possible.
recommendations.reason: HRV data is missing but essential for recovery calibration; breathwork improves parasympathetic tone and may accelerate HRV rebound.

risk_flags.evidence: Aerobic TE >3.0 on three of last five runs (8.7, 8.9, 8.27), ground contact time ↑80+ ms on 8.23, cadence ↓13 spm from July peak (151 → 138), and complete absence of Z1 work this month
risk_flags.action: Pause all Z2+ running for 5 days; reassess after Zone 1 test run

weekly_focus.description: Prioritise vagal tone restoration and neuromuscular recovery over distance or pace; rebuild rhythm before load.
